o1.biggest_strength: It acts on all three signals in the data (dispatch silence, fit-finder reach, refund-first portal) and does the arithmetic openly, with a real expected range rather than one perfect number.
o1.biggest_mistake: It puts the fit-finder and portal fixes behind the tickets work even though bras are half of all returns and £139,800 of postage, so the biggest money lever is not first, and its quiz-return assumption is quietly generous.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Rank the three fixes by pounds saved and show why the fit finder (9,300 bra returns, 77% size-related) comes before or alongside the tickets, with the bra-size-switch swap as step one.

o2.biggest_strength: It gets the arithmetic right (6,076 day-3-to-5 tickets, 5,394 too-small returns, £14,852 saved) and names the two-day silence as the first, cheapest fix with a clean target table.
o2.biggest_mistake: It keeps the old delivery confirmation and treats the swap savings as cash kept (£209,600) rather than gross profit, and its email 2 depends on an order-change ability it only lists as 'to confirm'.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give every message the fit help in our own words and put a stop-or-skip rule beside each move, while showing swap savings net of the new-size postage.

reason: Output 1 feels more built around our actual customers and our voice, and it names what to stop; Output 2 is tidier on the numbers but its swap figure reads like sales kept rather than profit, so I'd trust Output 1's shape slightly more.
